Self-Concept

Self-concept — self-esteem, body image, role performance and factors affecting self-concept.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • Define self-concept and its components
  • Describe factors affecting self-concept
  • Explain how to support a patient's self-concept

In simple words

Self-concept is how a person sees themselves — self-esteem, body image and role. Illness, injury and hospitalisation can damage self-concept.

Nurses support self-concept by respecting the patient, encouraging independence and promoting a positive body image.

Components of self-concept

Component Meaning
Self-esteem How much a person values themselves
Body image How a person sees their own body
Role performance How well a person performs their roles (parent, worker)
Personal identity Who a person believes they are

Factors affecting self-concept

  • Illness, injury, disability.
  • Surgery (mastectomy, amputation, stoma).
  • Ageing, pregnancy, menopause.
  • Culture, religion, social status.
  • Criticism or praise from others.

Nursing care

  • Encourage independence in self-care.
  • Praise effort and progress.
  • Respect privacy and dignity.
  • Help the patient adapt to body changes (stoma, scar, amputation).
  • Encourage expression of feelings.

🔴 Respect dignity

Respect the patient’s dignity and privacy. Encourage independence and praise effort — this protects self-concept during illness.

Where the nurse uses this

  • Body changes — support patients with stomas, amputations, scars or mastectomy; teach self-care.
  • Independence — encourage self-care as able; do not do everything for the patient.
  • Communication — speak respectfully; avoid criticism; praise progress.
  • Privacy — provide privacy during procedures and personal care.
  • Refer — refer to counselling if the patient is severely distressed about body changes.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. Self-concept = self-esteem, body image, role performance, personal identity.
  2. Illness, surgery and injury can damage self-concept.
  3. Support self-concept by encouraging independence and praising effort.
  4. Respect privacy and dignity in all care.
  5. Help patients adapt to body changes (stoma, scar, amputation).

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Body image is how a person sees their own body.
  2. Role performance is how well a person performs roles like parent or worker.
  3. Criticism lowers self-esteem; praise builds it.
  4. Refer to counselling for severe distress about body changes.

📌 Memory trick

Self-concept parts: “S-B-R-I” — Self-esteem, Body image, Role performance, Identity.

60-second revision

  • Self-concept = self-esteem, body image, role performance, identity.
  • Illness/surgery can damage self-concept.
  • Encourage independence; praise effort.
  • Respect privacy and dignity.
  • Support adaptation to body changes.

Test yourself

Self-concept includes all except:

Answer: D. Blood pressure is not part of self-concept.

Body image is:

Answer: B. Body image is how a person sees and feels about their own body.

A mastectomy can affect a patient’s:

Answer: A. Surgery changing body appearance can damage self-concept and body image.

To support self-concept, the nurse should:

Answer: B. Encourage independence in self-care to protect self-concept.

Self-esteem is:

Answer: A. Self-esteem is how much a person values and respects themselves.
